This week concludes unsupervised learning: **hierarchical clustering** (building dendrograms from a distance matrix) and **Principal Component Analysis (PCA)** for dimensionality reduction. Use the language toggle above to switch between R and Python.

<!-- R quizzes -->
<div class="lang-r">

<h3>Quiz 1: Hierarchical Clustering <span id="quiz-done-w4_q_hclust" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What is the key difference between k-means and hierarchical clustering?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc1" id="hc1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc1a">They are mathematically identical, just different function names</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc1" id="hc1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc1b">K-means requires the number of clusters upfront; hierarchical clustering builds a dendrogram you can cut at any level afterwards</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc1" id="hc1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc1c">Hierarchical clustering can only be used on 2 variables at a time</label></div>
    <div id="hc1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What property must a distance matrix always have, e.g. for use in <code>pheatmap()</code>?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc2" id="hc2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc2a">It must be symmetrical — the distance from A to B equals the distance from B to A</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc2" id="hc2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc2b">It must only contain values between 0 and 1</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc2" id="hc2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc2c">It must be based on Euclidean distance only</label></div>
    <div id="hc2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> Why do we often select only the top 25% most variable genes before clustering samples?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc3" id="hc3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc3a">To reduce file size only, it has no effect on the analysis</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc3" id="hc3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc3b">Low-variance genes barely differ between samples, so they add mostly noise rather than useful signal</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="hc3" id="hc3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="hc3c"><code>pheatmap()</code> cannot handle more than 100 rows</label></div>
    <div id="hc3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkHclustQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="hclust-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 2: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) <span id="quiz-done-w4_q_pca" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What is the main goal of PCA?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc1" id="pc1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc1a">To remove every correlated variable from the dataset</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc1" id="pc1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc1b">To reduce dimensionality by finding new, uncorrelated variables (principal components) that capture as much variance as possible</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc1" id="pc1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc1c">To impute missing values automatically</label></div>
    <div id="pc1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> In <code>prcomp(bc_data, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)</code>, why do we scale the data?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc2" id="pc2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc2a">Scaling is mandatory syntax with no statistical purpose</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc2" id="pc2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc2b">So variables measured on larger numeric scales don't dominate the PCA just because of their range</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc2" id="pc2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc2c">So the data gets converted to ranks, like Spearman correlation</label></div>
    <div id="pc2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does a scree plot show?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc3" id="pc3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc3a">The pairwise correlation between all original variables</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc3" id="pc3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc3b">How much variance each principal component explains, usually shown in decreasing order</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pc3" id="pc3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pc3c">The cluster assignment of each patient</label></div>
    <div id="pc3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkPcaQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="pca-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 3: Putting it together <span id="quiz-done-w4_q_together" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> In the PCA loadings (<code>pca_result$rotation</code>), what does a large positive value for a variable on PC1 mean?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt1" id="pt1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt1a">That variable has too many missing values</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt1" id="pt1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt1b">That variable contributes strongly and positively to PC1</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt1" id="pt1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt1c">That variable is uncorrelated with everything else</label></div>
    <div id="pt1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> How can PCA be combined with k-means clustering?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt2" id="pt2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt2a">They cannot be combined</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt2" id="pt2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt2b">Run k-means on the first few principal components (<code>pca$x</code>) instead of the original variables</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt2" id="pt2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt2c">PCA replaces the need for clustering entirely</label></div>
    <div id="pt2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What is one key difference between what hierarchical clustering and PCA each produce?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt3" id="pt3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt3a">Hierarchical clustering produces a dendrogram/tree of similarity; PCA produces new continuous axes (components) that summarize variance</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt3" id="pt3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt3b">They always produce exactly the same plot</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="pt3" id="pt3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="pt3c">PCA only works on categorical data, clustering does not</label></div>
    <div id="pt3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkTogetherQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="together-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

</div><!-- end .lang-r -->
